### Halo Wars 2 (`hw2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation, before any `hw2` unit is coded, from Halopedia's ten Halo Wars 2 building pages (Firebase, Banished outpost, UNSC Barracks, UNSC Garage, UNSC Airpad, UNSC Armory, Banished Raid Camp, Banished Foundry, Banished Apex, Banished War Council), a sample of its unit pages (Cyclops, Wolverine, Reaver, Wraith, Jackrabbit, Scarab, G81 Condor, Marines), its Halo Wars 2, Phoenix Logs and Season 0 to 15 pages, and Halo Alpha's Wraith, Banshee, Ghost and Phantom pages.

- **Where official text is.** No Halo Wars 2 manual was found (Halopedia has a manual page only for Halo Wars), and Halo Waypoint's Halo Wars 2 game page answers HTTP 500. Official text comes from three places: the in-game production tooltip, the Phoenix Logs (the in-game codex) and the patch notes.
- **The production tooltip** ([Halo Wars 2](https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2), Gameplay, Units) gives each unit a type line that names its own role (Anti-Air, Mobile Artillery and the like, in place of the killer roles of Halo Wars), a description of a few short phrases, and four counter icons. Halopedia copies the first two in two places: the Type and Description columns of the table on each building page, and the Info line in the Halo Wars 2 part of most unit pages, which usually includes the type. Neither says what it copies, but the same pages credit their quote boxes to the in-game description, the Foundry table marks a slip in the Marauder's text with [sic], and Halo Alpha quotes the same phrases for the Wraith and the Ghost. Read both as copies of in-game text, with two cautions.
  - **Dates differ.** Unit pages and Halo Alpha mostly show launch or beta text and prices; the building tables are later but not current throughout (see the research notes on prices). The Ghost is fast moving in Halopedia's Banished outpost table but very fast moving in Halo Alpha's quote.
  - **Copy errors in the Type column.** The Scorpion and the Gauss Cannon upgrade are typed Core Aircraft ([UNSC Garage](https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Garage)), and the Chopper is typed Light Infantry with a price of nothing ([Banished outpost](https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost)).
- **Roles step 1: the type line is the designation.** Read the Type cell of the unit's row on its building page, and check it against the type in the unit page's Info line and, where one exists, Halo Alpha's Purpose line. A role counts when every copy that names a role names the same one; skip a cell that is a plain copy error. Every unit has a type line, so step 1 never falls back to the description.
  - Type words that name a role: Anti-Infantry gives anti-infantry. Anti-Vehicle Mech or plain Anti-Vehicle gives anti-armour, through the alias anti-vehicle; Anti-Air, Anti-Air Vehicle or Anti-Air Mech gives anti-air; Mobile Artillery gives siege, through the alias artillery, and siege's coding rule still applies; Scout, Scout Vehicle or Scout Mech gives scout; Support Unit gives support only when the stock unit meets support's requires (the Nightingale and the Banished Engineer heal and repair; the Shroud, the Frostraven and the Methane Wagon do neither, so step 1 skips support for them).
  - Words that name no role: Core Infantry, Core Vehicle, Core Aircraft, Core Air, Core Mech, Core Tank, Main Battle Tank, Heavy Tank, Heavy Mech, Heavy Air, Light Infantry, Mobile Garrison, Super Unit, Hero Infantry, Hero Vehicle, Hero Mech and Hero Unit. Anti-Building (Jump Pack Brutes, Elite Enforcers, Grunt Riders) and Anti-Building Mech (Locust) name none either: anti-building is not a label or alias of siege in the word list, so it is a question for the rule-fix round; the step 3 siege test can still give siege.
  - Names: the Sniper's name names its job, so official text calls it a sniper (marksman at roles.secondary step 1, when its weapon reaches long). The Banished Engineer is a Huragok that heals and repairs; its name names the engineer role only if it builds or takes over structures, and the Apex table says neither.
- **Descriptions, patch notes and Phoenix Logs** count for roles.secondary step 1 and for strong and weak wording.
  - A description phrase that names a job counts: each Mobile Garrison can transport infantry (transport).
  - The patch notes on Halopedia's Season pages copy the official Halo Waypoint forum posts, each one cited there. They often name a unit's job: [Season 6](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_6_(Halo_Wars_2)) groups the Cyclops and the Hunters as anti-vehicle units; [Season 10](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2)) treats Wolverines and Reavers as AA and wants scouts to beat rush infantry and lose to core infantry; [Season 11](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_11_(Halo_Wars_2)) calls the Elite Rangers an anti-infantry unit of tier 2.
  - [Phoenix Logs](https://www.halopedia.org/Phoenix_Logs) says its entries are copied word for word from the game, and each unit page draws in the unit's entry. An entry opens with a short line (the Wraith's: heavy mortar tank) and then tells the machine's story. It is official text, but not the designation; the infobox role field that cites a log is the wiki's summary.
- **Strong against and weak against.** The tooltip has no Strong vs. or Weak vs. line. Its four icons grade the unit against infantry, vehicles, aircraft and buildings: green for good, yellow for okay, red for poor and none for a kind it cannot attack; heroes show them too ([Halo Wars 2](https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2), Units). Pages report the grades in words: Halopedia's unit-page prose uses the same scale (does well or is effective, okay, poor, cannot attack), and Halo Alpha's Attack Strength list uses Good, Moderate and Poor or Weak. Read a good grade as official strong-against text for roles step 4, and a poor grade as a weak point for the roles.secondary drop rule, only when a page gives the grade for that unit on that scale; cite the page. Okay and Moderate are neither. When two reports disagree, use neither and add an uncertain entry with sources_disagree. A few descriptions have wording of their own: the Reaver page's Info line calls it weak against vehicles. Wording on an upgrade or an ability (Canister Shell strong against infantry, Scorch Mortar strong against ground targets, Plasma Torpedo much stronger against aircraft) belongs to that part only and never counts at roles step 4 for the stock unit.
- **Game data bonus (roles step 4).** The patch notes give some damage modifiers from the game data: core aircraft against tier 3 tanks and the Colossus at 1.3 since 2 April 2018 (Season 10, Global), and the Jackrabbit against scouts at 1.7 since 18 July 2018 (Season 11). Count a modifier above 1.0 only when a note gives its value for the unit's current main weapon and no later note changes it; a change given only in per cent does not show a value above 1.0.
notes.game_wide:
### Halo Wars 2 (`hw2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation, before any `hw2` unit is coded, from Halopedia's Halo Wars 2 page (Gameplay), its ten building pages, its Resources, Garrison, Power Node, Leader power, Leader, Active camouflage, Energy shielding, Red Team, Phoenix Logs and Season 0 to 15 pages, and the leader pages of Captain Cutter and Commander Jerome. Standard skirmish and multiplayer only: Blitz plays with cards instead of bases and stays out.

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): every unit. Move, attack, attack-move, queued orders and hold position (the last three added on 26 September 2017: [Season 7](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_7_(Halo_Wars_2)), Control improvements), select all, and control groups. A unit's own special ability on the Y button is not an order: record it on the unit (the patch notes speak of the Wraith's and the Brute Grenadiers' Y abilities, Seasons 1 and 14).
- **Veterancy** (earn-veterancy; leave it off): units rank up three times, each rank lifting attack and defence; a Spartan riding a hijacked vehicle can climb to six, and the hero requirements were raised in June 2017 ([Halo Wars 2](https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2), Units; [Season 4](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_4_(Halo_Wars_2)), Hero Veterancy). No page read says how ranks are earned or shows a rank adding a weapon or a button, so no unit links earn-veterancy; a unit with rank bonuses of its own (the Brute Grenadiers' extra damage and protection per rank, Season 15) says so in notes. Leader powers that speed up ranking (Battle Hardened), promote units in an area (Field Promotion) or drop units that are already ranked are side-wide.
  - Exception: the strategy part of Captain Cutter's page says Battle Hardened works for every unit but the Nightingale, which hints that the Nightingale never ranks up. A coder of a unit that does no damage (Nightingale, Banished Engineer, Shroud) checks its own pages and adds an uncertain entry.
- **Unit upgrades** (Paired entries): the building tables list each unit's upgrades under the building that researches them (rows typed New Ability, Unit Upgrade or Weapon Upgrade). Record what each adds, with source upgrade. No page read says whether an upgrade also reaches units already in the field, so link upgrade-in-field only where a cited page shows that, and otherwise add an uncertain entry at the ability or weapon; the merge pass sets the batch's line.
- **Army and base upgrades** (side-wide; leave them off): Infantry, Vehicle and Air Upgrades I to III (more damage and health for the whole class, at the Barracks or Raid Camp, the Garage or Foundry, the Airpad or Apex), and, at the Armory or War Council, Fortify Base, Advanced Logistics (faster production) and Reinforcements (a higher population cap). Bands use the stock unit.
- **Leader powers and privileges** (side-wide): every leader has ten powers on a radial menu, unlocked one at a time with leader points earned in play ([Leader power](https://www.halopedia.org/Leader_power), Halo Wars 2), and a privilege that changes whole classes (Cutter's faster infantry, Jerome's stronger units at low population). Leave them off. A power that gives named unit types a new button or effect is recorded on each of them, with source commander-power: UNSC Raid II lets Jackrabbits capture points ([James Cutter/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/James_Cutter/Gameplay)). A power that only changes numbers (Battle Hardened, Time for Heroes, Recon Sight) is not an ability. A power that adds a death effect (Kinsano's Hellcharge, Season 15) goes in on_death.notes.
- **Units that a leader power brings.** A unit that a leader point unlocks for purchase at the Firebase or Outpost (Protector Sentinel, Mastodon, Frostraven, Skitterer, Phantom, Methane Wagon, Wraith Invader) is a unit of its own: its gate is the tech level in the table, and tier.basis names the power. A unit that only a power drops onto the field (ODSTs from ODST Drop, Omega Team, Decimus from Decimus Drop, the Retriever Sentinel, the Pelicans of Close Air Support, the Lich of Lich Vanguard) is a call-in with no gate in the tier_map: leave it out unless the trim and the registry add one.
- **Capturing points** (no pattern; leave it off): only infantry take a Forerunner Power Node, once its Sentinel guards are dead, and the node then yields power ([Power Node](https://www.halopedia.org/Power_Node), Halo Wars 2). capture-structure does not fit, since the nodes are neutral. Units whose description calls them quick capture units (Marines, Grunt Squad, Heavy Grunts, Cannon Fodder) say so in strengths. Turning an enemy-held point back to neutral (Can de-capture, on the Jackrabbit and the Chopper) is not game-wide: record it on those units with a fit_note, as no registered pattern fits.
- **Garrison towers** (carry-passengers on the building; leave it off the units): most multiplayer maps have Forerunner Garrison towers that hold one infantry unit, giving it cover and more range and sight ([Garrison](https://www.halopedia.org/Garrison)). Entering and leaving are universal keys; range and sight bands use the unit outside.
- **Mobile Garrisons** (Paired entries): the Mastodon, Phantom and Wraith Invader carry infantry that fire from inside (their table rows), so each keeps one seat passive linking passenger-sets-weapon. Loading and unloading are universal keys. Seat counts come from the rows: the Mastodon three, four with Infantry Capacity; the Phantom two, three with Gunboat Capacity.
- **Hijacking and commandeering**: not game-wide. Only the Spartan heroes do it, through their Hijack upgrade, which takes enemy vehicles and aircraft and boards friendly ones ([UNSC Armory](https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Armory); [Red Team](https://www.halopedia.org/Red_Team), Halo Wars 2). Record it on them: hijack-vehicle for the enemy side; for boarding a friendly vehicle, test join-ally-crew's summary.
- **Cloak and detection**: a cloaked unit cannot be targeted until a detector reveals it ([Active camouflage](https://www.halopedia.org/Active_camouflage), Halo Wars 2). Cloaking belongs to the unit that does it: the Active Camo upgrades of the Sniper and of the Shipmaster's and Arbiter's Grunts, the Honor Guard, and the Shroud's field (the cloak pattern, on each). A unit hidden only by a Shroud, a Cloaking Generator or a leader power gets no cloak. Detection is the sensor trait detector on each unit whose description says it detects cloaked units (Sniper, Wolverine, Nightingale, Reaver, Elite Rangers, Banished Engineer); the Jackrabbit, Chopper and Ghost detect only after an upgrade, so put that in sensors.notes. Since 2 April 2018 a detector reveals cloaked units out to its base line of sight, whatever the high ground ([Season 10](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2)), Global). Sensor Towers and Cloaking Generators are buildings.
- **Shields** (armour model regen-shield, per unit): some units carry an energy shield, among them the Wraith from the start (its page) and the Spartans. The Spartans' shields recharge after a pause ([Red Team](https://www.halopedia.org/Red_Team), Changes from Halo Wars), and Commander Jerome's Info line has a fast-recharging shield; no page read says so for vehicle shields. Code regen-shield on a unit whose own sources give it a stock shield, with an uncertain entry at armour/models when no page shows that shield recharging; a shield that only an upgrade adds goes in armour.notes. Base shields belong to buildings.
- **Healing** (none game-wide): units do not heal by themselves; the Marines lost their healing out of combat ([UNSC Marine Corps/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Marine_Corps/Gameplay), Changes). Units that heal or repair others record repair-allies (Nightingale, Banished Engineer, the Marines' Combat Tech upgrade, Pavium). Healing leader powers (Restoration Drones, Atriox's Bulwark) and Colony's privilege are side-wide. Code self-repair only where a unit's own stock sources show it healing itself.
- **Population** (side-wide; no pattern): units take population, from a cap of 80 that the Armory or War Council raises to 120 ([Resources](https://www.halopedia.org/Resources), Halo Wars 2); heroes take none.
- **Heroes** (availability unique): each leader has one hero, bought at the Armory or War Council at tech 1 (most for 300 supplies and 275 power), with a limit of one active hero ([Jerome-092/Gameplay](https://www.halopedia.org/Jerome-092/Gameplay), the Spartan's Info line). In multiplayer a dead hero is bought again, never revived ([Red Team](https://www.halopedia.org/Red_Team)). Each hero upgrade raises health and damage and adds one ability or weapon: record the added part with source upgrade, and put the health and damage in notes.
- **Super units** (availability open unless a page shows a cap of their own): the UNSC Condor and the Banished Scarab (the Volatile Scarab for Voridus) cost 2,000 supplies, 2,000 power and 40 population at tech 3. The Scarab page allows up to three at once in standard modes, which is also all that the top population cap leaves room for; add an uncertain entry at availability.
- **Ramming**: not game-wide. A unit whose description or patch notes show a ram (Warthog, Flame Warthog, Ghost, Grunt Riders; the Chopper in Seasons 10 and 15) records it on itself. The rams of Choppers, Ghosts and Warthogs, and the Scarab's stomp, share one damage type, and a rammer takes back part of the damage it deals ([Season 10](https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2)), Global).
- **Crates** (picking one up is a universal key): supply and power crates lie on the map for units to collect ([Resources](https://www.halopedia.org/Resources)). Leave them off; a unit that gathers faster says so in strengths (Grunt squads gather faster since Season 2).
- **Sight** (no pattern): fog of war covers the map, and high ground raises a unit's line of sight but not its detection range (Season 10, Global). Sight bands use flat ground.
- **Squads** (crew model squad): infantry are sold as squads (Marines come four to a squad). Upgrades that only add members (Pack Brother, Dark Skies, New "Recruits", Squad Reserves, Arbiter's Champion) change numbers: notes. An added member with a weapon or job of its own (the Marines' Combat Tech, with a rocket launcher and repairs) is an upgrade weapon or ability.
- **Base features** (leave off): locking down a Firebase or Outpost to hold trained units inside, turrets and their upgrades, Sensor Towers, Cloaking and Shield Generators.
- **No crushing found**: no page read shows vehicles running over infantry outside a ram; give crush only where a unit's own page shows it.

registry_findings.current: The final balance update of 13 August 2020 (Season 15; 343 Industries announced in February 2021 that no further balance patches would follow), standard skirmish and multiplayer values (not Blitz), as given by Halopedia in October 2026. Tech 1 is mapped t1 on the assumption that the UNSC, like the Banished, starts a match with HQ tech 1; no source found says so for the UNSC, and if it starts at tech 0, its tech 1 units are t2
registry_findings.proposed: "The final balance state of Season 15: the patch of 13 August 2020 and its follow-up of 4 September 2020, which changed only Kinsano's Hellcharge leader power (343 Industries said in February 2021 that no further balance patches would follow). Standard skirmish and multiplayer values (not Blitz). Halopedia's building tables are not tied to one patch, so each price is checked against the patch notes on its Season pages, newest first. Tech 0 and tech 1 are both t1: the Banished open with a Stronghold (HQ tech 1), and the patch notes treat tier 1 as the opening tier for both sides (Season 4 names tech-0 scouts and a tech-1 hero's Mantis as tier 1; Season 6 names the tech-2 vehicles tier 2 and the tech-3 tanks tier 3); no page states the UNSC start in so many words."
registry_findings.evidence: https://www.halopedia.org/Season_15_(Halo_Wars_2) (Season 15 Title Updates): two patch tabs, 13 August 2020 and 4 September 2020; the second only retunes Kinsano's Hellcharge. https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/lovely-letters (HALO WARS 2 part): rules out further balance patches and dates the latest to the August before. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_1_(Halo_Wars_2) (March 20 patch, Units) sets the Jackrabbit at 200 + 12 (it was 220 + 15) and the Wraith at 525 + 70 (it was 550 + 40), while https://www.halopedia.org/Firebase and https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_Foundry (HW2 tables) still give 220 + 15 and 550 + 75; other rows do carry late values (Vulture power 100 and the Frostraven and Protector Sentinel prices from August 2020), so the tables mix patches. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_4_(Halo_Wars_2) (June 29 and July 7 notes) calls the tech-0 Jackrabbit and Chopper tier 1 units and wants Jerome's Mantis beatable at tier 1; https://www.halopedia.org/Season_6_(Halo_Wars_2) (August 17 patch) names Warthog, Flame Warthog, Mantis and Marauder as tier 2 vehicles and Scorpion, Wraith, Colossus and Grizzly as tier 3. https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost (In-game information, Stronghold bullet) gives the Stronghold as the starting base, and https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_Apex (In-game information) says the tech-1 Apex can go up at the start; the Firebase page states nothing about the UNSC start.

registry_findings.current: Price = supplies + power, counted at par: no source gives income rates, and units are paid mostly in supplies while power mostly buys tech and upgrades. Anchor: the two main battle tanks, the UNSC Scorpion (550 supplies, 90 power) and the Banished Wraith (550 supplies, 75 power), about 630 (the mean is 632.5); thresholds at 0.5, 0.9, 1.4 and 2 times the anchor, rounded to the nearest 10. Leader-power and Blitz card prices are not unit prices.
registry_findings.proposed: Keep low 320, medium 570, high 880 and very-high 1260; replace the basis with: "Price = supplies + power, counted at par: no source gives income rates, and units are paid mostly in supplies while power mostly buys tech and upgrades. Anchor: the two main battle tanks, the UNSC Scorpion (550 supplies, 90 power) and the Banished Wraith (550 supplies, 75 power), about 630 (the mean is 632.5); thresholds at 0.5, 0.9, 1.4 and 2 times the rounded anchor of 630, rounded to the nearest 10. The Wraith's price is uncertain: the Banished Foundry table gives 550 and 75, but the last Wraith price change in the patch notes (Season 1, 20 March 2017) set 525 and 70, and no later note changes it; with 525 + 70 the anchor would be 617.5 and the thresholds 310, 560, 860 and 1,240, which would move the Colossus (870) to high and the Phantom (315) and the Grunt Goblin (310) to low, so such units get an uncertain entry at cost_band. Leader-power and Blitz card prices are not unit prices."
registry_findings.evidence: https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_Foundry (HW2 table): Wraith row 550 supplies, 75 power. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_1_(Halo_Wars_2) (March 20 patch, Wraiths): price changed to 525 and 70. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2) (May 14 balance patch): the Wraith gets building damage and shield increases with no price change, while the Scorpion drops from 600/90 to 550/90 and the Grizzly from 900/140 to 850/140; no other Season page changes the Wraith's price. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_4_(Halo_Wars_2) (June 28 notes) says a service-side balance update would follow that the notes leave out, so unlisted changes exist and the table may still be right. The stored 880 and 1260 come from 630 x 1.4 and 630 x 2; from 632.5 they would be 890 and 1270, the figures in the step-1 note. Prices used for the flipping units: Colossus 750/120 (https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Garage), Phantom 225/90 (https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost), Grunt Goblin 175/135 (https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_War_Council).

registry_findings.current: Marines (the UNSC core infantry squad trained at the Firebase). No source found gives movement speeds as numbers, so speed bands come from the in-game descriptions ('very fast moving', 'slow moving') and patch notes, at lower confidence.
registry_findings.proposed: "Marines (the UNSC core infantry squad trained at the Firebase). No source gives the Marines' speed as a number, so no unit has speed_raw. The official patch notes (Halopedia's Season pages) give a few speeds on the game's own scale: Banshee 20.5 (2 April 2018), the classic Spartan heroes 15 (17 August 2017), Hunters 12 and Shroud 11 (8 February 2018), Jump Pack Brutes 11 (18 April 2019) and Vulture 11 (16 December 2019). A speed word in the in-game description sets the band of the same name: Very fast moving gives very-fast; Fast moving and Fast movement speed give fast; Slow moving, Slow speed, Slow movement speed and Slow and Tough give slow. A unit with no speed word is judged from those figures and from units with words, with an uncertain entry; where two copies of a description disagree on the word, take the band nearer medium and mark the uncertain entry sources_disagree."
registry_findings.evidence: https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2) (April 2 patch, Cleansing Beam): Banshee speed 20.5 given as a reference. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_6_(Halo_Wars_2) (August 17 patch, classic Spartans): speed 13 to 15. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_9_(Halo_Wars_2) (February 8 balance patch): Hunters 11 to 12, Shroud 10 to 11, Hornet raised to the Wolverine's speed. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_12_(Halo_Wars_2) (April 18 balance patch): Jump Pack Brutes 12 to 11. https://www.halopedia.org/Season_14_(Halo_Wars_2) (December 16 patch, Vultures): 9 to 11. No Season page gives a Marine figure. The speed words appear in the Description columns of the building tables (for example https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Garage and https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_War_Council) and differ between copies (Ghost fast in https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost, very fast in https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Zaagokelu_Workshop_Scout_Bike). The speed-bands description in docs/vocabularies.md lets a speed word set the band of the same name only where the registry says so, naming Halo Wars 2, so the registry text should spell out the reading; the step-1 note's 'fast or very fast' for very fast moving does not match that rule.

registry_findings.current: None: no source found gives sight figures (the patch notes give only some changes in per cent), so every sight band is a medium proposal
registry_findings.proposed: "None: no source gives the Marines' line of sight, so every sight band is a medium proposal. The patch of 2 April 2018 (Season 10) set each detector's detection range to its base line of sight on flat ground and lists them on the game's own scale: Engineer and Nightingale 65, Elite Rangers 70, Chopper, Reaver and Wolverine 75, Ghost and Jackrabbit 80, Sniper 90. High ground raises sight but not detection. sensors.notes may compare these units in words."
registry_findings.evidence: https://www.halopedia.org/Season_10_(Halo_Wars_2) (April 2 patch, Global, Detect Range Increase): detection ranges set equal to each unit's base line of sight on flat ground and fixed there, unaffected by the cliff rule that raises sight; then the old and new range of the Engineer, Elite Ranger, Chopper, Ghost, Reaver, Nightingale, Sniper, Jackrabbit and Wolverine. The Chopper, Ghost and Jackrabbit detect only with an upgrade (https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost and https://www.halopedia.org/Firebase tables), and https://www.halopedia.org/Season_11_(Halo_Wars_2) (July 18 patch) moved the Jackrabbit's extra sight onto its spotter drone. No page gives a Marine figure, so the bands stay medium proposals; the wording of the current entry is what is wrong.

notes.other_notes:
- **Step-1 statements that no longer hold** (checked on 11 November 2026):
  - The cost tables of the Banished infantry and air buildings are on Banished Raid Camp and Banished Apex; Halopedia has no Banished Hall or Banished Summit page (Hall and Summit are Covenant buildings of Halo Wars).
  - "No numeric speeds": the patch notes give a few speeds on the game's own scale, though none for Marines (registry finding on speed_reference).
  - "Very fast moving means fast or very fast": the speed-bands description says a game word read as a band gives the band of the same name, so where the registry allows the reading, very fast moving is very-fast.
  - Thresholds 890 and 1,270: the registry stores 880 and 1,260, worked out from the rounded anchor of 630.
  - Jackrabbit 235: the table's 220 + 15 came with the patch of 7 March 2017 (Season 0), and the patch of 20 March 2017 lowered it to 200 + 12 (Season 1), with no later change listed. The band stays very low.
  - "Heroes about 575": most heroes cost 300 + 275, but Pavium costs 350 + 275 (625) and the Grunt Goblin 175 + 135 (310, very low).
  - "Season 15 (August 2020) is the last": its page also holds a patch of 4 September 2020 (Kinsano's Hellcharge only).
  - The Banished outpost page still says a match opens with a Stronghold, but that section copies Firebase text (its quote box names the Combat Station); weigh it with the Banished Apex page, where the Apex needs tech 1 yet may go up as soon as play begins.
- **Open points, settled as far as the pages allow:**
  - **UNSC start.** No page says outright that the UNSC opens with HQ tech 1. The official patch notes treat three tiers with tier 1 as the opening: Season 4 calls the Jackrabbit and the Chopper (tech 0 in the tables) tier 1 units and wants Jerome's Mantis (from an Armory hero, tech 1) beatable at tier 1; Season 6 names the tier 2 vehicles (Warthog, Flame Warthog, Mantis, Marauder, all tech 2) and the tier 3 tanks (Scorpion, Wraith, Colossus, Grizzly, all tech 3). With the Banished pages, this supports the tier_map for both sides.
  - **Speeds in numbers:** six units have one in the patch notes, Marines none (registry finding).
  - **Halopedia prices:** not one patch. Many rows match the last price change in the Season pages, but some keep launch prices or match no listed change: the Jackrabbit, the Cyclops (its own page has the March 2017 price, 120 + 120), the Reaver (the April 2018 notes give 175 + 215, as does its page), the Hunters, the Elite Rangers, the Suicide Grunts and the Wraith. For cost_band.raw, take the newest dated price (the latest patch note that changes it, otherwise the building table) and give the other in an uncertain entry. Unit pages and Halo Alpha mostly hold launch or beta prices: take no price from them.
  - **Leader units:** faction unsc or banished, no subfactions. A leader's unit with its own in-game name is a unit of its own (Grizzly, Mantis, Colossus, Flame Warthog, Cryo Troopers, Elite Enforcers, Grunt Riders, Heavy Grunts, Cannon Fodder, the Ghost of the Shipmaster and the Arbiter, the Volatile Scarab and the leader-power units). Name the leader, and the standard unit it replaces, in tier.basis; availability stays open. Set variant_of only when a source names a standard unit as its base (the Flame Warthog to the Warthog; the Volatile Scarab to the Scarab, whose page covers both); a unit that only replaces another (the Grizzly for the Scorpion) gets none. A unit that keeps its standard name under every leader (the Grunt Squad, which the Shipmaster and the Arbiter lead with an Elite and other upgrades) is one unit, with the leader's version in notes. The units of Pavium and Voridus get introduced_in hw2-awakening-the-nightmare (the expansion's page says it added both leaders); the other DLC leaders came through the season pass and get none.
- **Page names.** In-game names are short (Wraith, Cyclops); page titles are lore names: Eklon'Dal_Workshop_Wraith, HRUNTING_Mark_III_(S)_Cyclops, M9_Wolverine, Dovotaa_Workshop_Reaver, M121_Jackrabbit, Barukaza_Workshop_Scarab, G81_Condor, UNSC_Marine_Corps/Gameplay. Follow the link in the Name cell of the building table. Ids follow the Name cell (Grunt Squad gives grunt; Jump Pack Brutes gives jump-pack-brutes).
- **Version traps.** The Halo Wars 2 part of a unit page often shows launch values (the Jackrabbit page lists a weapon upgrade that the June 2017 patch made standard; the Cyclops page's Info line says fast moving, the Barracks table has no speed word). Halo Alpha's blocks are mostly beta or launch (Scorpion 390 + 120, Reaver 235 + 100, Banshee at tech 1). Check every value against the Season pages, newest first.
- **Tech levels to watch.** The Cyclops, Hunters and Elite Rangers need tech 2 although their buildings are open from the start (t2). The Banished Apex needs tech 1 while the UNSC Airpad needs tech 2, so the Banished Engineer is t1 and the Nightingale t2.
- **Armour class, step 2** (the game's own armour word). The patch notes name the armour type of some units: Season 6 counts the Warthog, Flame Warthog, Mantis and Marauder as Medium units and the Scorpion, Wraith, Colossus and Grizzly as Heavy units, and Season 10 names the members of its light armored type (in its words: Flamers, Cryo Flamers, Suicide Grunt, Brute Rider and Brute Grenadier). Read these first. Otherwise the description's armour word decides when it is light or heavy, with very or a word form ignored: Light armor (Sniper, Jackrabbit, Chopper, Ghost, Wolverine, Reaver, Locust), Very light armor (Skitterer), Heavy armor (Cyclops, Scorpion, Grizzly, Wraith, Vulture, Blisterback, Hunter Captain), Heavily armored (Hunters), Very heavy armor (Condor, Scarab; check A then applies). Tough armor (Marauder, Mantis) is not a class word. Joined-up names in the notes (HeavyInfantry, MediumAA, MediumHero, lightrush) are internal names, like Red Alert 3's armour sets, not armour words. No armour_map: no page gives every unit's type.
- **Speed words.** Fast moving is misspelt Fast moiving in the Garage table; Slow and Tough (Pavium) counts as slow. Where two copies differ on the word (the Cyclops, the Ghost), take the band nearer medium and mark the uncertain entry sources_disagree. The patch-note figures help judge units with no word: Banshee 20.5, classic Spartan heroes 15, Hunters 12, Shroud 11, Jump Pack Brutes 11, Vulture 11; the Hornet was raised to the Wolverine's speed (8 February 2018, no figure), and Commander Jerome lost a quarter of his base speed (August 2020).
- **Range words.** The descriptions grade reach in words (Very long range, Long range, Medium range, Mid-range missiles). With no figures, the range tie-break takes the band the source names: long for long or very long, medium for medium or mid-range.
- **Matchups in official words.** The patch notes state intended matchups: scouts beat rush infantry and lose to core infantry (Season 10); infantry are meant to answer aircraft (Season 9 on the Elite Rangers, Season 10 on Marines and Grunts against aircraft); aircraft beat vehicles (Season 10, Global); the Cyclops and Hunters counter the tier 2 vehicles (Season 6).
- **Lineage.** Halo Wars (`hw1`) is in this batch, so check each unit against it: the same name and the same job (the Warthog, Scorpion, Wolverine, Hornet, Wraith, Ghost and Banshee, among others) gives the Halo Wars slug as lineage. Halopedia's UNSC Barracks page links the Halo Wars Flamethrower row to its Hellbringers page, so those two share one as well.
- **Flood and Sentinels.** The registry's flood faction is AI only, outside version_researched's skirmish and multiplayer scope, so a Flood unit would rest on campaign or Firefight values; the trim should leave it out or say so. The Aggressor Sentinels that guard Power Nodes are neutral guards, not a side; Anders's Protector Sentinel and Retriever Sentinel are UNSC units.
- **Sites to cite** (one page each for the copy-check site test): www.halopedia.org, https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Garage (a building table, In-game information); halo.fandom.com (Halo Alpha), https://halo.fandom.com/wiki/Eklon'dal_Workshop_Mortar_Tank; www.halowaypoint.com (official news), https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/lovely-letters (its old Halo Wars 2 game page and three 2017 posts answered HTTP 500). Read the patch notes through Halopedia's Season pages, which cite archived copies of the forum posts.
- **Cost.** HW2 prices need a check against up to sixteen Season pages per unit; those pages, the ten building pages and the mechanic pages above are now in the page cache, so reuse them.
- **Copy-check of these texts:** run offline against the 1,483 pages it could read (the whole cache plus every linked page), with no shared run of six words left.

The outpost page's own table and bullet price the Stronghold as a 400-power upgrade from tech 0 and its Phoenix log has the Outpost upgraded into a Stronghold; the Firebase page calls the base the default starting Firebase and prices the Combat Station as a tech-0 upgrade. The findings rewrite version_researched but leave both notes stating one side of a disputed point.

Cannon Fodder and Shroud prices: https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost charges Cannon Fodder 100 supplies, but its own description calls it free and https://www.halopedia.org/Halo_Wars_2 (Leaders paragraph) says Yapyap recruits it without spending resources; the Chopper row's type (Light Infantry, the first phrase of Cannon Fodder's description) and empty price look like Cannon Fodder's values, and the Chopper's last listed price is 245/15 (Season 1, 20 March 2017). The Shroud's row (400+60) matches no listed change either (Season 6, 17 August 2017, gives 550 to 450). Bands stay the same, but cost_band.raw and the price-trap list should cover them.

More official job names in the patch notes (roles.secondary step 1): https://www.halopedia.org/Season_9_(Halo_Wars_2) (8 February 2018, the note that raises the damage of core tier 2 air against vehicles) says air units are intended as one of the army's anti-vehicle answers, naming anti-armour through its alias anti-vehicle for core air (Hornet, Banshee); Season 6 (17 August 2017, Reaver) says the bug fix makes the Reaver work as an anti-air unit; Season 11 (18 July 2018, Voridus) gives his Grenadiers the right weapon type to be actual anti-infantry. The role_line's examples cover only the Cyclops, Hunters, Wolverines, Reavers and Rangers.

Light Infantry as a game word: the patch notes use it as a damage target class (Season 8: Suicide Grunts deal more damage to Light Infantry; Season 15: infusion and Grenadier damage against light infantry cut), and it opens Cannon Fodder's in-game description. The armour-class step 2 notes do not say whether it counts as the game's own word light (it would make Cannon Fodder light rather than unarmoured) or which units it covers.

Wraith Phoenix log: https://www.halopedia.org/Phoenix_Logs/Banished_Units/Wraith (official text) describes the Wraith as a mainline tank that is also an artillery piece, so official text names siege's alias artillery for the Wraith at roles.secondary step 1; the role_line cites only the log's opening line and calls the infobox's artillery wording the wiki's summary.

Veterancy details: Season 11 (18 July 2018, Forge and Pavium) normalizes the XP each veterancy rank needs, so ranks come from XP thresholds (what earns XP is not stated); Season 8 (Voridus, Pack Assault) drops a veteran Infused Engineer, so a unit that does no damage can hold a rank.

Hijacking limits: https://www.halopedia.org/Jerome-092/Gameplay (Halo Wars 2 prose) says Commander Jerome cannot hijack, and the UNSC_Armory Hijack row covers only Jerome-092, Alice-130 and Douglas-042; the same page's Strategy part has the Omega Team call-in hijacking.

Queued orders predate Season 7: Season 1 (20 March 2017, Gameplay) fixes Shift + right-click waypoints that sometimes failed, and Season 6 (17 August 2017, Buildings/Units) fixes a bug that kept commands from queuing for Spartans riding hijacked vehicles.

A power income figure exists: Season 6 (17 August 2017, Economy) lowers the power income of the map's Energy Capture Points from 2 to 1.5 per second, so the cost basis should say that no source gives supply income rates.

candidates.teaches: Boarding as a skill. The Spartan slams down onto an enemy vehicle or aircraft, an EMP pins it in place, and he takes it over while it stays stuck; killing him before he finishes cancels the takeover. He can also climb into a friendly vehicle to boost it. Iconic counter: keep anti-infantry units next to your armour.

candidates.shooter_note: A tough hero on foot with a pistol: leap off a ledge onto an enemy tank or gunship, freeze it and wrestle the driver out while your team covers you; jump into a friendly vehicle to make it stronger.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009) has the same line: its Red Team Spartans already hijack enemy vehicles, commandeer friendly ones for better stats and walk out of a wreck unhurt (Red_Team, Halo Wars section). The sequel adds the Spartan Slam (crossing heights, area damage, a stun when boarding), the EMP that freezes the target, aircraft as targets (Armory table), one hero per leader with its own level-2 weapon, and hijack as a bought upgrade. In the data, hijack-vehicle is Jarmen Kell's crew snipe from range (Generals) and join-ally-crew is the Line Officer (Tempest Rising); both pattern files already cite these Spartans as other examples.

candidates.name: Condor (G81 heavy gunship, the UNSC super unit)
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (the page rates it well against vehicles, aircraft and structures, only fair against infantry)
candidates.teaches: The super-unit tier as a flying fortress: 40 population, 2,000 supplies and 2,000 power, very heavy armour, guns that engage several targets at once, and a Mini MAC shot with a small blast. Its twist is a weakness built in: the shells are slow, so fast units such as Ghosts, Hornets and Banshees dodge them, and it needs escorts.

https://www.halopedia.org/UNSC_Armory (Halo Wars 2 table: the Condor row)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, every UNSC leader, tech 3. The Condor page says it is built at the Firebase while Halopedia's Armory table lists it under the Armory: check. The Blitz version, which stays 60 seconds, is out of scope.
candidates.shooter_note: A team-scale flying fortress: slow, huge and very hard to bring down from the ground, it rakes several targets at once and fires a slow Mini MAC round on a cooldown; agile fliers and buggies dodge it, so it needs fighter cover.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit; Halopedia dates the G81 gunship to 2559, the Halo Wars 2 era. In the data, fire-power-shot is Anna Kos's (Iron Harvest) and the registry's Yamato Cannon example; a slow, very tough flier recalls the RA3 Kirov, but the Condor is a gunship that cannot hit fast targets.

candidates.name: Jackrabbit (M121 scout vehicle)
candidates.role_guess: scout (its table type is Scout Vehicle)
candidates.teaches: A cheap, very fast scout whose job is the map, not the fight: it undoes enemy captures and gathers resources as other scouts do, and its one upgrade adds a support drone that repairs it, widens its sight, reveals cloaked enemies and shoots. A helper drone bought as an add-on that keeps a fragile scout alive.

https://www.halopedia.org/MQ-96_Support_Drone
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, every UNSC leader, at the Firebase, tech 0. Campaign and multiplayer differ: the campaign one starts unarmed and has its own Mini-frag launcher upgrade, while in multiplayer it has carried a grenade launcher from the start since the June 2017 balance patch. Price conflict: 220 supplies and 15 power on the Firebase table, 350 and 15 on the Jackrabbit page's multiplayer column (very low or low band).
candidates.shooter_note: The cheapest, fastest UNSC ride: race around to flip enemy capture points back and grab crates; with the upgrade a small drone orbits you, patches your hull, shows cloaked enemies and plinks at targets.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit; the first game's UNSC scout was the Warthog (Firebase, Halo Wars table). In the data, the Generals Technical is the cheap, very fast raider, and launch-drones comes through the Drone Operator and Vimana (Tempest Rising); here it is one lasting helper bought as an upgrade. Undoing captures is a capture-point rule (no pattern), and crate collection may be game-wide for Halo Wars 2 scouts: the game notes decide.

candidates.name: Colossus (Mark II (J) heavy mech, Sergeant Johnson's)
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (its long railgun is not a sniper-family weapon)
candidates.teaches: A heavy walker that splits its jobs across two guns fired together: an autocannon that hits everything, aircraft included, and a heavy railgun that reaches ground targets from very far away. Its upgrade adds Stomp, a ground shock that stuns and hurts enemy ground units near it: the answer to infantry at its feet.

new_mechanics.summary: On a key, slam the ground to stun and damage every enemy ground unit close around you; fliers are untouched. The Spartan Slam's stun when it lands on a vehicle to board it is a second Halo Wars 2 case.

candidates.shooter_note: A slow, towering walker with two weapons on one trigger: an autocannon for anything near, fliers too, and a railgun that picks off ground targets from across the map; when infantry swarm its legs, a stomp knocks them out for a moment.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit; it arrived with Sergeant Johnson as a Halo Wars 2 leader. Heavy walkers in the data are Iron Harvest's (the Kaiser, the Stark); none has a stunning stomp.

candidates.role_guess: anti-infantry or area-denial (rated good against infantry and buildings)
candidates.teaches: Fire as terrain: an exosuit hero with twin flamers and a quickly recharging shield draws a wall of fire across the ground that burns anything moving through it, with larger walls at its top upgrade. A hazard shaped as a line, which cuts a lane in two; it cannot hit aircraft. Class note: an exosuit, coded infantry like Iron Harvest's William Mason, unless the researcher judges it a vehicle on legs (walker).

candidates.shooter_note: A shielded flamethrower suit that lays walls of fire across chokepoints: enemies who walk through burn, so you choose where the fight can go; aircraft are out of your reach.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009) has a Cyclops line (Forge's building-killer exosuit with a repair-kit upgrade, Firebase Halo Wars table) but no flame hero or fire wall. In the data, leave-hazard-zone is the RA2 Desolator's radiation; the wall shape is the twist.

candidates.name: Protector Sentinel (Forerunner flier under Professor Anders)
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (the page rates it well against vehicles) with disabler from its stun bolt
candidates.teaches: An AI machine on the human side: a Forerunner flier with a sustained beam that, once upgraded, flies with two smaller Aggressor Sentinels as escorts and gains a targeted Lockdown Bolt, a shot that stuns and hurts what it hits; at the top upgrade it detonates when destroyed, and its EMP burst slows the units around it. https://www.halopedia.org/Firebase (Halo Wars 2 table: the Protector Sentinel and Drone Escort rows)

candidates.shooter_note: A hovering Forerunner drone with a steady beam, two small wingman drones and a stun bolt to pin a target; when it dies, a slowing EMP pulse punishes whoever dived it.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit; Anders fielded the Gremlin and the Hawk there (Firebase and Airpad, Halo Wars tables). In the data, launch-drones comes through the Drone Operator and Vimana; the death pulse is an on_death detail, not a pattern.

candidates.name: Scarab (Banished super unit)
candidates.role_guess: assault (the page rates it well against structures, vehicles and infantry)
candidates.teaches: The super-unit walker: it hits very hard, has very heavy armour, crosses any terrain, and on a key a plasma shield makes it invulnerable for a few moments. A player may have three on the field together in normal play, and it is only fair against aircraft, so air is the counter. Three Skitterers can ride one.

https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_War_Council (Halo Wars 2 table: the Scarab and Volatile Scarab rows)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, every Banished leader except Voridus (he gets the Volatile Scarab, whose beam leaves pools of infusion gel; it has no page of its own), at the War Council, tech 3, 2,000 supplies and 2,000 power, at most three at a time. The Blitz version is out of scope.
candidates.shooter_note: A team's boss walker: it strides over cliffs, wrecks infantry, tanks and buildings, and on a key raises a plasma shield that makes it untouchable for a few seconds; aircraft are its weak side.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009) has the same line: a Covenant Scarab super unit whose weapon is a plasma cannon (the Halo Wars 2 section contrasts the two). The sequel adds the plasma-shield invulnerability, Thrasher missiles and the cap of three. In the data, become-invulnerable is the Generals Aurora Bomber's (untouchable while supersonic); the biggest walkers so far are Iron Harvest's.

candidates.name: Shroud (Banished support aircraft)
candidates.role_guess: buffer, or no role fits (it neither heals nor buffs in the word list's sense): researcher to check
candidates.teaches: A support flier with no weapon and two modes that exclude each other: deployed, it keeps a cloaking field over the units around it; otherwise its point defence knocks incoming enemy shots out of the air, two at a time. Hide the raid or shield it, never both; detectors reveal the cloak and a large volley gets past the defence.

new_mechanics.summary: An automatic point-defence system shoots down a few incoming enemy shells and missiles aimed at you and teammates close by; a volley bigger than its capacity gets through. If the sources show it guarding only the Shroud itself, use the interceptor armour model instead.

candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, every Banished leader, at the Apex, tech 2, 400 supplies and 60 power. Shipmaster can buy a wider, longer cloak with a leader point.
candidates.shooter_note: A flying support with no gun: park it to cloak your strike team, or keep it visible and its point defence swats incoming shells away from the group; you protect, you never shoot.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit. In the data, the RA1 Mobile Gap Generator hides allies with an always-on field (shroud-area); here the cloak is a deployed mode traded against point defence. The cloak pattern file already names the Shroud as an area example; the interceptor armour model protects only its owner.

candidates.name: Engineer (Huragok, Banished support flier)
candidates.teaches: A healer whose key button is a shield: it repairs or heals one target at a time, three times as fast as the UNSC Nightingale, and casts a temporary energy shield that cuts the damage taken by units inside; casts stack, each weaker than the one before. It cannot fight and it detects cloaked units, so enemies focus it. Class note: a floating living creature, so aircraft in low air rather than drone, which is for machines.
pages: https://www.halopedia.org/Huragok (Gameplay: the Halo Wars section, and the Halo Wars 2 Engineer and Infused Engineer entries)
https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_Apex (Halo Wars 2 table: the Engineer row)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, every Banished leader except Voridus (his Infused Engineer throws gel pools and has no shield), at the Apex, tech 1. Price conflict: 200 supplies and 30 power on the Apex table, 120 and 50 on the Huragok page (very low either way).
candidates.shooter_note: A floating, unarmed medic that mends one teammate at a time and throws an overshield bubble over the group; you also reveal cloaked enemies for the team, which makes you the first target.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009) has the same line: its Covenant Huragok repairs and heals, carries no weapon and cannot mend itself (Huragok, Halo Wars section). The sequel adds the stacking overshield and cloak detection. In the data, repair-allies comes through the RA1 Field Mechanic, the Shieldmaiden and others; no unit links raise-shield yet.

candidates.name: Skitterer (Colony's scout walker)
candidates.role_guess: scout, with buffer when it rides a host
candidates.teaches: Riding an ally as a turret: the cheap, fast scout walker clamps onto a friendly unit, adds to its health and keeps firing from it; it is destroyed only along with the host (rarely sooner), and the host's size sets how many fit (a Scarab three, a Hunter pair two, an Engineer one). On its own it is a light beam scout that can gather resources. Crewed by a colony of worms, so not the drone class.

new_mechanics.summary: Clamp onto a friendly unit as an extra turret: you add to its health and keep firing, ride wherever it goes, and die only when it dies; bigger hosts take more riders. join-ally-crew boards inside, one rider per vehicle, and throws the rider clear alive.

https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost (Halo Wars 2 table: the Skitterer row)
https://www.halopedia.org/Colony/Gameplay (the Skitterer leader power)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, for Colony only, at Banished outposts once the Skitterer leader power is bought, tech 1, 150 supplies and 20 power.
candidates.shooter_note: A cheap, fast crab-walker: scout and grab crates alone, then hop onto a teammate's tank or walker to ride it as an extra gun and armour plate; you are safe until your host dies, and you go down with it.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit. In the data, join-ally-crew is the Line Officer (Tempest Rising), who boards a vehicle to raise its rank; here the rider stays outside, adds health and keeps shooting, several per host. Yapyap's Grunt Riders (a Grunt on a Brute's back) are a looser cousin.

candidates.name: Methane Wagon (Yapyap's support wagon)
candidates.teaches: One cloud, two effects: an always-on methane aura makes nearby Grunts hit harder and take less damage while enemies inside deal less and lose armour, and the wagon lobs kegs that start the same cloud further off. It barely fights, yet the page says it usually beats a Marauder through its buffs and debuffs, and it explodes on enemies when destroyed. Class note: a modified Shadow, so hover may fit better than vehicle.

new_mechanics.summary: An always-on cloud around you makes your own troops of one kind hit harder and take less damage while enemies inside it hit softer and take more; shells you fire start the same cloud elsewhere. Voridus's Infused Engineer gel pools, which buff allies or hurt enemies, are a cousin.

https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_outpost (Halo Wars 2 table: the Methane Wagon and The Good Stuff rows)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, for Yapyap only, at Banished outposts once its leader power is bought, 300 supplies and 120 power (tech 1 on the outpost table, tier 0 on the unit page). If the kegs are its plain attack rather than a key, they take the weapon trait zone instead of leave-hazard-zone.
candidates.shooter_note: A rickety gas cart that rolls with your Grunt swarm: inside its cloud your squads hit harder and shrug off hits while enemies weaken; lob kegs to gas a chokepoint, and when it is destroyed it blows up on the enemies around it.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit. In the data, rally-allies comes through the Generals Overlord, the Line Officer and the Enlightened, and leave-hazard-zone through the RA2 Desolator; none weakens enemies with the same aura that strengthens allies.

candidates.name: Hunter Captain (Mgalekgolo Captain, Colony's hero)
candidates.teaches: The taunt: a slow, heavily armoured hero whose first upgrade makes nearby enemies attack nothing but it for a while (wider at tier 3, where taunted enemies also deal less damage), while every hit of its beam heals it. The first unit in the data for draw-fire.

https://www.halopedia.org/Phoenix_Logs/Banished_Units/Hunter_Captain (the in-game log text: a superheavy hero whose taunt pulls nearby enemy attacks onto itself to protect allies)
https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_War_Council (Halo Wars 2 table: the Hunter Captain and Taunt rows)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, for Colony only: a War Council hero at tech 1, 300 supplies and 275 power, one at a time.
candidates.shooter_note: A walking bunker: you are slow and huge, your beam heals you as it hits, and a taunt forces every enemy nearby to shoot only you while your team flanks them.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009) has Hunters but no Captain; the Captain, its taunt and its health-stealing beam are new. In the data, no unit links draw-fire yet; healing by hitting is the weapon trait heal-on-hit.

candidates.role_guess: support (repairs structures), with disabler from the slow on painted targets
candidates.teaches: Marking as a team multiplier: a slow, tough Brute hero who paints enemies so that they move slower and lose armour for everyone; upgrades make his shells paint what they hit, widen the paint and, at the top, give him a shield that sends damage back at attackers. He also repairs friendly structures, and he has healing drones whose rate each upgrade raises.

candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no such unit. candidates.role_guess: assault, with disabler from Hammer Stun
candidates.teaches: A melee brute who brings the fight to his hammer: the first upgrade fits the hammer with a gravity beam that hauls enemies toward him, the second makes his hammer blows stun in an area, and the third heals him with each hit. A pull-then-smash combo on foot.

https://www.halopedia.org/Banished_War_Council (Halo Wars 2 table: the Warlord and Hammer Pull rows)
candidates.skirmish: Yes, skirmish and multiplayer, for Decimus only: a War Council hero at tech 1, 300 supplies and 275 power, one at a time.
candidates.shooter_note: A gravity-hammer bruiser: yank a sniper or rocket trooper into reach with the gravity beam, then flatten the group with a stunning area smash; every blow heals you, but aircraft are beyond you.
candidates.repeats: Halo Wars (2009): no Warlord (Decimus first appears in Halo Wars 2); its Brute Chieftain leader unit, also a hammer brute, is the nearest line, for the judge to check. In the data, pull-target is the RA2 Magnetron lifting vehicles from range; here it feeds a melee fighter.

candidates.coverage_note: 14 candidates, 6 UNSC and 8 Banished: the Banished leaders' own units (Colony, Yapyap, Pavium, Decimus) teach more new mechanics than the UNSC's, whose core roster mostly repeats Halo Wars or the data. CLASSES: infantry 5 (Jerome-092, Kinsano's Cyclops as an exosuit, Hunter Captain, Pavium, Warlord), vehicle 2 (Jackrabbit, Methane Wagon, which may be hover as a modified Shadow), walker 3 (Colossus, Scarab, Skitterer), aircraft 4 (Condor, Protector Sentinel, Shroud, Engineer, a floating creature). No ships (Halo Wars 2 builds none); the Flood are AI-only and skipped. ROLES (guesses): scout (Jackrabbit, Skitterer), support (Engineer, Pavium), buffer (Methane Wagon, maybe Shroud), assault (Scarab, Hunter Captain, Warlord), anti-armour (Condor, Colossus, Protector Sentinel), anti-infantry and area denial (Kinsano's Cyclops), infiltrator (Jerome-092), disabler as a second role (Warlord, Pavium, Protector Sentinel). Not covered on purpose: anti-air primary (Wolverine, Reaver), marksman (the Sniper repeats Jarmen Kell), transport (Mastodon, Phantom and Wraith Invader repeat the fire-port garrisons of the Battle Bus and the Multigunner IFV), logistics (no harvester unit). TIERS: t1 10 (every hero is tech 1), t2 1 (Shroud), t3 3 (Condor, Scarab, Colossus); Halo Wars 2's tech-2 roster is mostly core units that repeat. PRICE BANDS (supplies + power against 320/570/880/1,260): very low 4 (Skitterer 170, Protector Sentinel 215, Engineer 230 or 170, Jackrabbit 235 or low at 365), low 2 (Methane Wagon 420, Shroud 460), medium 6 (heroes at 575 to 625, Colossus 870), high 0 (only Forge's Grizzly at 990 sits there, a Halo Wars line too), very high 2 (Condor and Scarab, 4,000 each). MECHANICS: fills three registry ids no unit links yet: draw-fire (Hunter Captain), mark-target (Pavium), raise-shield (Engineer); also hijack-vehicle by boarding, join-ally-crew, leap, fire-power-shot, launch-drones, become-invulnerable, cloak (area), repair-allies, rally-allies, leave-hazard-zone, pull-target, retaliate-on-hit, gather-resources and upgrade-in-field (hero and unit upgrades are researched for units already on the field). Four proposed ids: ground-slam (Colossus), latch-onto-ally (Skitterer), buff-and-curse-aura (Methane Wagon), point-defence-allies (Shroud, to confirm against the interceptor armour model). HALO WARS OVERLAP: the same line exists in both games for Jerome-092 (Spartans), the Scarab and the Engineer (Huragok); Kinsano's Cyclops shares only the Cyclops suit. The other ten are new in Halo Wars 2. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: Commander Jerome (his call-down Command Mantis, which an onboard AI runs when he is out, repeats Iron Harvest's William Mason); Kodiak and Blisterback (deploy-siege-mode repeats; the Blisterback is the RA2 Siege Chopper's air-to-ground deploy); Frostraven, Cryo Troopers and Bison (freeze-and-shatter repeats the RA3 Cryocopter, though the Frostraven does both halves itself); Nightingale (a second healer: three at once through drones, plus Defensive Smoke); Mantis (its designator paint overlaps Pavium); Suicide Grunts (Halo Wars holds the richer version, a suicide toggle with the Zeal speed upgrade); Grunt Goblin and Grunt Riders (overlap the Methane Wagon's Grunt buffs and the Skitterer's riding); Voridus, his Infused Engineer and the Volatile Scarab (gel pools repeat leave-hazard-zone); Arbiter, Honor Guard and Atriox's Chosen (rage and cloak repeat overclock-self and cloak); Forge's Warthog and Sgt. Johnson's Green Machine (aura and repair-beacon heroes that repeat rally-allies and deploy-turret); core units (Marines, Hellbringers, Warthog, Scorpion, Wolverine, Hornet, Vulture, Grizzly, Cyclops, Grunts, Jump Pack Brutes, Elite Rangers, Hunters, Ghost, Chopper, Marauder, Reaver, Locust, Wraith, Banshee), mostly shared with Halo Wars or generic. SITES to cite, one page each for the site test: www.halopedia.org (https://www.halopedia.org/Klavbrig_Workshop_Shroud; every page above, and the Season pages for patch notes, such as https://www.halopedia.org/Season_15_(Halo_Wars_2)); www.halowaypoint.com (https://www.halowaypoint.com/en-us/news/lovely-letters, the February 2021 post saying no more Halo Wars 2 balance patches would come; it read as text with the page reader). The official notes of the 13 August 2020 patch were a Halo Waypoint forum post that now answers 404, and its web.archive.org copy could not be reached here: if the batch cites web.archive.org, it needs its own plant test. Liquipedia is not needed for this game. The Volatile Scarab has no page of its own. Halopedia answered every request at once, with no 429.
